full_judgment:
Shushanto Kumar Das director of Dhaleashwari Ice and Cold Storage (Pvt.) Limited (the cold storage) obtained loan of Tk.5,02,83,000/- from Agrani Bank Limited (hereinafter referred to as the Bank)for construction of the cold storage. The cold storage was constructed with the loan sanctioned by the Bank and in additional to that the writ petitioners also inverted some Money for its construction. The Construction work of the cold storage was completed in 1994 and it started operation in 1995. The Bank also sanctioned Tk-2 crore as case credit loan to the writ petitioner failed to pay the installments of both the project loan as well as working capital loan (case credit limited) As a result the Bank on 19.06.2008 filed Artha Rin Suit No.02 of 2008 in the Artha Rin Adalat and Joint District Judge, 1st court, Munshigonj (hereinafter stated as the Adalat) for recovery of loan amount to Tk-18,38,03,249.87 impleading the writ petitioner and others as defendants of the suit. Defendant -writ petitioner contested the suit by filling a written statement. Finally the suit was decreed by the Adalat by judgment and decree dated 10.10.2012. The judgment-debtor writ petitioner failed to pay the installments in terms of the decree. Therefore, the Bank filed Artha Jari Case No. 2 of 2013 before the Adalat for recovery of the decrial dues. In the execution case notice was published in the daily newspaper, Shokaler Khabar dated 25.05.2013 for appearance, of the judgment debtors in the execution case. The writ petitioner without complying with the terms and conditions of the decree then filed writ petition No.7723 of 2013 before the High Court Division challenging the notice dated 25.05.2013 published in the daily Shokaler Khabar dated 25.05.2013 which was published for appearance of the judgment debtors inArha Jari Case No. 02 of 2013within 09.06.2013 . The Bank Contested the rule by filling an affidavit-in-opposition clearly stating that the suit was legally decreed infamous of the Bank that the writ petitioner having failed to pay the first installment of decrial dues within 10.11.2013 the Bank legally filed Artha Jan Case No. 2 of2013 following the pro-visions of section 49(3) read with section 28 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 that the writ petition is not maintainable and the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 d) It has already been settled by the Appellate Division in the case reported in Bangladesh  Agri cultural Development Corporation (BADC) Vs Artha Rin Adalat and ors 59 DLR (AD) 6, Gazi M Towfic Vs Agrani Bank and others 54 DLR (AD) 6, that the Judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat Cannot be interfered with by the High Court Division in writ jurisdiction . But the High Court Division interfere with judgment and decree passed by the Adalat that too violating the provision section 50 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 8. It appears that from the materials on record that admittedly Artha Rin Suit No.2, of 2008 was decreed against the writ petitioner by the Adalat. The judgment debtor-writ petitioner failed to pay the installment of decrial dues as per the judgment and decree passed by the learned Judge of the Adalat. Therefore, the Bank filed the execution case before the Adalat. 

 10. It is not the case of the judgment—debtor writ petitioner he paid the first installment in terms of the judgment and decree. Therefore the execution case was legally filed by the Bank in compliance case was legally filed by the Bank in compliance with the provision of section 49(3) read with section 28 and 29 of the Ain. The notice was published in the newspaper for appearance of the judgment —debtors following the provision of section 30 of the Ain in a newspaper. The notice was for information to the judgment- debtors that a execution case has been filed for non-payment of decree dues. Therefore the notice was published about filing of the execution case legally. Further, the High Court Division had no jurisdiction to interfere with the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in writ petition by directing the writ petitioner only to pay the principal amount of loan without paying the interest.
